direct_answer:
Aker BP conducted its double materiality assessment (DMA) initially in 2023 in line with CSRD/ESRS and revised it in 2024 based on new information, implementation guidance and EFRAG’s draft oil & gas sector standard [Source 1]. The DMA maps impacts, risks and opportunities (IROs), their dependencies, and how they connect to Aker BP’s own operations and its upstream/downstream value chain, considering activities, business relationships and geographies [Source 1].

Methodologically, Aker BP applies a systematic approach covering both impact materiality (inside-out impacts on environment and society) and financial materiality (outside-in financial risks/opportunities, including reputational risk and dependencies on natural, human and social resources) [Source 2]. It uses a structured, iterative four-step process: (1) define business context (activities, business model, value chain, stakeholders, boundaries), (2) identify actual and potential IROs using top-down and bottom-up approaches with internal/external stakeholder input and quantitative sources, (3) assess and prioritise IROs against impact and financial materiality criteria using a standardised rating system, and (4) validate through management/Board review, report outcomes, and monitor for updates when circumstances change [Source 9].

The IRO assessments use severity × likelihood ratings aligned with the enterprise risk management approach (consequence × probability), using company scales and the same tool as other company risks so that IROs are prioritised and handled together with other risks [Source 2]. Special attention is given to dependencies between impacts and corresponding risks/opportunities [Source 2].

Stakeholder engagement is incorporated: Aker BP maintains dialogue to identify risks, opportunities and actual/potential impacts, including public consultations for project impact assessments (e.g., PDOs) and a whistleblowing channel [Source 3]. Stakeholder perspectives were included in the DMA through in-depth interviews and workshops with internal management and subject matter experts, and the 2024 process built on prior-year interviews involving owners, key suppliers, customers, NGOs and authorities [Source 3]. Governance-wise, all material IROs identified were reviewed by the Board of Directors (BoD), Audit and Risk Committee (ARC) and Executive Management Team (EMT) [Source 6], and ARC/EMT are kept informed about affected stakeholder views through channels including the DMA approval process and integrity channel cases [Source 2].

In determining where material matters arise, Aker BP focused its own-operations assessment on oil and gas production as the activity with the highest potential for material impact; upstream value chain material topics mainly relate to development projects due to significant construction activity; and downstream impacts relate to the use of petroleum products [Source 1]. Aker BP notes it is still improving its understanding of the value chain with suppliers/partners and will update the DMA as new relevant information becomes available [Source 1].
compliance_rationale: The report describes that the DMA covers both impact and financial materiality, includes mapping of IROs and dependencies across own operations and value chain, uses a structured multi-step process with identification, assessment/prioritisation, validation and monitoring, and incorporates stakeholder perspectives and governance review [Source 1] [Source 2] [Source 3] [Source 6] [Source 9]. However, the passages do not provide full detail on specific thresholds/criteria for determining materiality, the exact scoring scales, or how impacts are assessed for severity dimensions (scale, scope, irremediability) as expected under ESRS impact materiality guidance; therefore evidence is not sufficient to conclude high compliance based solely on the provided excerpts.

key_findings: First DMA conducted in 2023 under CSRD/ESRS; revised in 2024 using new information, implementation guidance and EFRAG draft oil & gas sector standard [Source 1].
DMA maps IROs, dependencies and links to own operations and value chain; considers activities, business relationships and geographies [Source 1].
Covers both impact materiality (inside-out) and financial materiality (outside-in), including reputational risk and dependencies [Source 2].

Uses a structured, iterative process: define context; identify IROs (top-down/bottom-up, stakeholder input, quantitative sources); assess/prioritise via standardised rating; validate by management/Board; monitor and update [Source 9].
IRO assessment uses severity × likelihood aligned with enterprise risk management and documented in the same tool as other risks [Source 2].

Stakeholder perspectives incorporated via dialogue, public consultations for impact assessments, whistleblowing channel, and interviews/workshops; prior-year interviews included owners, suppliers, customers, NGOs and authorities [Source 3].
All material IROs reviewed by BoD, ARC and EMT; ARC/EMT informed of stakeholder views through DMA approval process and integrity channel cases [Source 2] [Source 6].

Own operations focus on oil and gas production; upstream value chain focus on development projects/construction; downstream impacts relate to use of petroleum products; company is still improving value chain understanding and will update DMA as information improves [Source 1].
